text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned waking up frightened; can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes, such as whether you speak incoherently, have rapid eye movements, or appear paralyzed?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors (Sleep Terrors).

The clinical picture of an 8-year-old with sudden nocturnal awakenings characterized by screaming and crying, followed by rapid return to baseline without confusion, is highly characteristic of night terrors. Given the two-month history and frequency, this fits the diagnostic criteria without requiring further testing at this time.
